helper.modelBasics: Start with object basics first, then enable mainline behavior only when the type really belongs in topology.
helper.advancedMainline: Only resource types that should participate in the business mainline topology need mainline settings.
helper.mainlineNotice: Mainline types require scope, level, and a parent mainline type. Attaching under module is still not supported in P1.
helper.propertiesJson: Use JSON to add arbitrary properties. name / sort_order will be merged automatically.
helper.parentNodeEmpty: No eligible parent node was found under this business. Create the parent mainline instance first.
helper.instanceBusinessScope: Business-scope mainline instances usually require selecting a business before choosing a parent node.
helper.instanceListNote: Instance operations are still type-driven, but they are no longer the primary focus of the type detail view.
helper.instanceHistoryPage: Select an instance first, then inspect its history, relations, and topology context.
helper.instanceRelationsPage: This tab shows real instance-level relation data rather than type-level relation design.
helper.instanceRelationCreate: When creating an instance relation, the available target type and association type are constrained by type relation definitions.
helper.instanceConfigBlock: Configuration fields come from instance configs.
helper.instanceMetricsBlock: State fields come from instance state.metrics.
helper.instanceTopologyPage: Current topology contains {{nodeCount}} nodes and {{edgeCount}} edges.
helper.enumValues: Enum values will be used as dropdown options in the instance form.
helper.instanceFallbackForm: This type has no custom attributes yet, so the drawer falls back to the basic instance fields.
helper.attributeDesigner: Define type attributes first, then let the instance form render from that schema.
helper.attributeRoadmap: This round focuses on attribute structure and ordering. Drag layout, field grouping, and composite unique rules come next.
helper.attributeSortHint: Fields are currently ordered by sort_order. Drag sorting and field grouping will come in the next phase.
helper.listOverview: Resource types are now grouped first. Mainline is treated as one capability of a type, not the only center of the experience.
helper.groupsPending: Persistent type groups will be connected after the backend adds storage support. This round only establishes the IA and grouped browsing.
helper.groupsPage: Type groups now persist in the backend and can be used to organize both browsing and creation flows.
helper.previewNotice: The preview reuses the dynamic instance form mapping so schema changes can be validated immediately.
helper.relationsPending: Type relation design is not wired to the frontend yet, so this tab is a placeholder for now.
helper.relationsDesign: Type relations define which target types the current type can connect to, along with mapping and delete constraints.
helper.relationsDesignHint: This page manages type-level relation design only, not concrete instance-to-instance links.
helper.relationsListNote: These definitions directly constrain which instance relations can be created later. Check active usage before deleting.
helper.historyPending: This tab will later show type and attribute change history.
helper.uniquesPending: Composite unique rules, auxiliary uniqueness, and conflict feedback depend on the next backend validation pass, so this entry is reserved for now.
helper.uniquesDesign: Unique rules run before instance writes and prevent duplicate resources from entering the type.
helper.uniquesDesignHint: Default rules usually represent the primary identity, while auxiliary rules add business-specific duplicate constraints.
helper.uniquesListNote: Updating unique rules changes later create and update behavior. Check existing data for conflicts before editing.
helper.importExportPending: This tab will later host type import/export and template capabilities.
